loText: Describe debt value adjustment (DVA) and bilateral CVA (BCVA).
question: Northern Star Bank (NSB) and Horizon Financial Group (HFG) entered into a 4‑year interest rate swap in which NSB pays a fixed rate of 4.5% and receives 6‑month SOFR plus a spread. Since inception, both entities’ credit ratings have improved: NSB’s credit spread fell from 90 bps to 40 bps and HFG’s from 130 bps to 100 bps. Assume the SOFR curve is unchanged, so the exposure profiles (EPE and ENE) of an identical 4‑year swap initiated today are the same as at inception. Which of the following statements is most likely correct for the new swap?

options.A: Because NSB’s spread fell by more than HFG’s, NSB’s DVA will decrease and HFG’s DVA will increase.
options.B: Because NSB’s spread fell by more than HFG’s, NSB’s CVA will decrease and HFG’s CVA will increase.
options.C: Because both spreads fell, the CVA and DVA recorded by each party will be lower in magnitude.
options.D: Because both spreads fell, the CVA and DVA recorded by each party will be higher in magnitude.

solution:
**Step by step**

1. Each party’s CVA is driven by the counterparty’s spread: CVA $\approx-\text{spread}_{cp} \times$ EPE.
2. Each party’s DVA is driven by its own spread: DVA $\approx\text{spread}_{own} \times$ ENE.
3. NSB’s CVA depends on HFG’s spread (130 ‑> 100 bps, lower); NSB’s DVA depends on NSB’s own spread (90 ‑> 40 bps, lower).
4. HFG’s CVA depends on NSB’s spread (lower); HFG’s DVA depends on HFG’s own spread (lower).
5. With exposures unchanged, all four adjustments shrink in magnitude. How much each spread fell relative to the other has no bearing on the direction.

**REBUILT** — Original asked about ’DVA and CVA on both sides’ loosely; stem now fixes that exposure profiles are unchanged so only the spread effect is tested, and the options are worded in terms of magnitude.
